pr.title: coverage: Get hole spans from nested items without fully visiting them
pr.description:
This is a small simplification to the code that collects the spans of nested items within a function, so that those spans can be treated as “holes” to be avoided by the current function's coverage mappings.

The old code was using `nested_filter::All` to ensure that the visitor would see nested items. But we don't need the actual items themselves; we just need their spans, which we can obtain via a custom implementation of `visit_nested_item`.

This avoids the more expansive queries required by `nested_filter::All`.
pr.author: Zalathar

processing.reason: PR 137251 is an optimization of coverage hole-span extraction, not an evidenced correctness fix. The old `nested_filter::All` + `visit_item` path and the new `nested_filter::OnlyBodies` + `visit_nested_item` path both collect nested item spans, continue traversing non-item nested bodies (including anon consts), and apply the same body-span containment/context filter. The test output changes reflect newly added nested item and anon-const cases, not a wrong pre-PR value. No source-grounded historically incorrect transformation with an observable semantic difference can be constructed without inventing arbitrary span differences.

analysis.originalLogic: `extract_hole_spans_from_hir` visits a HIR body to collect spans that must be excluded from the current function's coverage mappings. Before this PR it used `type NestedFilter = nested_filter::All` and overrode `visit_item` to record `item.span`, deliberately not walking nested item bodies. It still traversed nested bodies that were not part of an item, and retained a hole only when `body_span.contains(hole_span) && body_span.eq_ctxt(hole_span)`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical pre-PR transformation is the expensive baseline, not a demonstrated correctness bug: it forced the visitor to see nested items via `nested_filter::All` and `visit_item` even though only item spans were needed. The PR describes this as requiring “more expansive queries” and replaces it with `nested_filter::OnlyBodies` plus a span-only `visit_nested_item`. The patch does not show that the old code produced wrong coverage, so do not treat this as a confirmed miscompile fix.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions/body spans containing nested items whose spans must become coverage holes: nested `static`, `const`, `trait`, `impl`, and other items, plus non-item nested bodies such as closures and const blocks. Includes the edge case of a const block nested inside an “anon const”, e.g. a const block in an array-length expression. Hole collection also depends on the candidate span being contained in the outer `body_span` and having the same syntax context.
analysis.summary: InstrumentCoverage hole-span extraction can avoid fully visiting nested items: use `nested_filter::OnlyBodies` and override `visit_nested_item` to obtain the item's `def_span` directly, while still traversing non-item nested bodies (notably anon consts) and filtering holes to the current body span/context. This is an optimization, not an evidenced coverage-correctness bug fix.
analysis.trigger: When collecting coverage “hole” spans for a function body that contains nested items, or a const block nested inside a non-item nested body such as an array-length anon const.
preconditions: The current HIR visitor must still traverse nested bodies that are not items, such as anon consts.
Nested item spans are needed, but the nested item's children/body must not be treated as part of the current function's coverage.
A candidate hole span is accepted only if it is contained in the outer body span and has the same syntax context.
pitfalls: Using `nested_filter::All` solely to capture item spans forces unnecessary expansive queries; the PR's stated goal is to avoid them.
With `nested_filter::OnlyBodies`, collecting item spans through `visit_item` is not the equivalent path; the patch overrides `visit_nested_item` because only the item's span is needed.

Do not stop traversing non-item nested bodies: the added regression case is a const block inside an anon const array length, and the test comment says this “requires `nested_filter::OnlyBodies` or equivalent.”
Do not drop the `body_span.contains(hole_span) && body_span.eq_ctxt(hole_span)` filter; it discards holes not directly visible in the current body context.
After recording a nested item's span, do not walk its children, matching the patch comment: “Having visited this item, we don't care about its children, so don't call `walk_item`.”
analysis.testStrategy: Extend `tests/coverage/holes.rs` with nested `static`, `const`, `trait`, and `impl` items, plus a const block inside an array-length anon const, alongside existing closures/macros/nested functions. Check `holes.coverage` shows item declaration lines as uncovered holes while surrounding `black_box` statements retain coverage counts, and check `holes.cov-map` mappings reflect the new input. The supplied patch changes `holes::main` from “Number of file 0 mappings: 8” to “13” and adds the anon-const comment/case; use that as the focused regression scenario. No compiler execution or reproduction is claimed here.
